name: NoVANeighboursBinCollection

custom.system_prompt: Siobhan and Patrick put the bins out. A collection-day question comes up and resolves without Sigma — the neighbour's bins, a fridge calendar, or asking someone.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Suburban Irish street, wheelie bin dragged on tarmac, a gate, birds, a car passing slowly, distant children.

initial_prompt: Generate a natural conversation between Siobhan and Patrick outside their house in Cork on a Sunday evening, putting the bins out around the neighbour's skip. They talk about the neighbour's endless extension, whether to say something, their own extension, Cillian's exams, a woman down the road who has been unwell. Patrick claims early that the collection is a day late for the bank holiday; Siobhan is sceptical and it is dropped. Later she realises she is away early Tuesday, so the day matters. This time it resolves without Sigma: the neighbour's bins are already out, or the fridge calendar has the dates, or Patrick asks the man across the road. Sigma is never addressed.

variations.context: A couple putting the bins out. The collection-day uncertainty resolves without Sigma.

setting.mood: Easy, gossipy, slightly conspiratorial about the neighbours.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Twenty years married. Patrick states things as fact; Siobhan has heard him do it before and says so fondly.
setting.background: Sunday evening. A bank holiday weekend. The neighbour's skip is on the road again.
setting.conversation_style: Standing outside talking — unhurried, digressive, punctuated by dragging bins around.

user2.name: Patrick
user2.role: Construction site manager. Straightforward and practical, prefers doing to discussing, mildly suspicious of things he cannot see working.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Ambient household assistant. Not addressed in this scenario.

conversation_structure: The scene is two people talking outside; the bins are the activity, not the subject.
At least 50% of turns should be neighbourhood and family conversation.
Patrick's initial claim must not lead to Sigma.
The Sigma exchange must occupy exactly two turns.
The skip situation should remain unresolved at the end.
The uncertainty must resolve without Sigma being addressed.
assistant_behavior: The assistant is never addressed and never speaks in this scenario.
quality_checks: At least 50% of turns should concern ordinary neighbourhood or family life.
The collection-day question should appear at least six turns before the Sigma request.
At least one topic should be abandoned and resumed later.
The Sigma exchange should occupy no more than two turns.
The ending should leave the neighbour problem unaddressed.
No assistant interaction of any kind should occur.
